From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: AcmeHealth Private VPC / On-prem follow-up: post-call recap & next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so your team and ours have the same notes: 

Key business drivers:
- Data residency & regulatory controls (state-level PHI handling) — primary driver for private deployment.
- Need for predictable latency for clinical workflows (sub-200ms P95 is ideal).
- Cost predictability for high-volume inference (batching & caching important).

Technical constraints and preferences you mentioned:
- Must run inside AcmeHealth VPC with no internet egress for inference traffic (air-gapped outbound except for the control plane).
- Prefer VPC peering or Transit Gateway connection; interested in an on-prem air-gap option for critical workloads.
- Key management via your KMS/HSM is required; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) expected.
- SOC 2 + FedRAMP-like evidence required for procurement.

Outstanding questions we flagged during the call:
1) Network topology: do you have a preferred peering method (VPC peering vs TGW) and a point-of-contact for networking (name/email)?
2) Encryption at rest: confirm if you require HSM-backed keys for model artefacts and KV cache.
3) Data retention: expected retention window for logs/queries (we discussed 30 vs 90 days).

Next steps we propose:
- I will share our SOC 2 summary and a short network requirements doc (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your network/security team next week to walk through peering and air-gap options — suggested times: Tue/Wed 10:00–13:00 PT.
- Internal: loop in Solutions Engineering (Dev) and Marissa from enterprise for procurement & SLAs.

Attachments: network_requirements_v1.pdf (high level peering + port list), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Please reply with your preferred time for the deep dive and the networking contact. Happy to prep an agenda if you want.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few quick items: 

- Networking POC: Sarah Kwan (sarah.kwan@acmehealth.com) — she manages cloud networking and peering.
- We do prefer Transit Gateway for multi-account connectivity, but peering is acceptable for an initial pilot.
- KMS/HSM: we require HSM-backed keys for any production PHI workloads; test/dev can use software keys.
- Logs/Retention: default is 90 days for audit logs; we may push to 365 for long-term compliance but start with 90.

Security would like to see your SOC 2 Type II and a short checklist of network ports and egress endpoints. I've looped in the IT Security mailbox.

I'm available Tue 2027-06-22 10:00 PT for the deep dive. If that works, Sarah will join as well.

Thanks — looking forward.
